validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: strongly confirmed, independent of GEM. Sea Robin is a heavily-litigated FERC-jurisdictional (Natural Gas Act) interstate gas transmission system offshore Louisiana -- confirmed by: (1) Sea Robin Pipeline Co. v. FERC, 127 F.3d 365 (5th Cir. 1997), a published federal appellate opinion reciting FERC's own factual findings about the system (found live via Wayback capture of caselaw.findlaw.com after the wiki's own casetext.com cite died 410 and law.justia.com 403'd scripted access); (2) Panhandle Eastern Pipe Line Co., LP FY2020 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed by the pipeline's current parent) which lists 'Sea Robin' by name as one of PEPL's three FERC-certificated transmission subsidiaries; (3) an Energy Transfer PHMSA-facing operator fact sheet hosted at pipelinesafetyinfo.com, naming 'Sea Robin Pipeline Company' and its Louisiana parishes of operation; (4) Wikipedia's 'Sea Robin Pipeline' article (the gem.wiki page's own citation, a bit.ly link, redirects here) corroborating route and ownership lineage; (5) a Southern Union Co. 2005 SEC press release confirming Sea Robin was an operating asset assessed for Hurricane Rita damage. CLASSIFICATION: correctly an interstate gas TRANSMISSION pipeline (not gathering) per the court's holding upholding FERC's transportation, not gathering, classification for NGA jurisdiction purposes. DUPLICATE: checked against the 37-pipeline roster -- no other row plausibly describes the same physical Ship Shoal-to-Erath system; not a duplicate/relabel. ATTRIBUTION (Operator/Owner): Operator 'Sea Robin Pipeline Co LLC' confirmed by the PEPL 10-K and the pipelinesafetyinfo.com fact sheet (2 independent, both name the entity exactly) -- REFS_ADDED, tier=high. Owner 'Panhandle Eastern' 100% confirmed by two independent sources naming Sea Robin explicitly and tracing the same ownership chain: the PEPL 10-K ('PEPL's subsidiaries are Trunkline, Sea Robin and Southwest Gas') and a contemporaneous Oil & Gas Journal article (23 Dec 2002, 'CMS Energy sells wholesale trading, gas pipeline units') naming 'CMS Sea Robin Pipeline Co.' as part of the Panhandle unit sold to Southern Union -- which merged into Panhandle Eastern Pipe Line Co. in 2014 per the chain Wikipedia/Fitch describe, landing back at today's Panhandle Eastern ownership. REFS_ADDED, tier=high. Opened and read to exhaustion: the court opinion, the PEPL 10-K, the pipelinesafetyinfo.com PDF, the Wikipedia article (both rendered and raw wikitext), the 2002 and 2000 OGJ articles, the 2005 Southern Union SEC press release, and the Federal Register/justice.gov filings named in the harvested pool. Of the 12 harvested wiki citations, 9 were opened and read (bit.ly/Wikipedia redirect, SEC 10-K, casetext [dead, 410], Hart Energy [live only via Wayback meta], justice.gov brief, pipelinesafetyinfo.com PDF, the two OGJ articles, Fitch [live but does not name Sea Robin -- fails the name-must-be-present rule, not usable]); 3 were not fully read (annualreports.com ETP 2022 PDF -- now 404, dead; Bloomberg snapshot -- 403, paywalled/blocked; Crain's Detroit -- 403, blocked, though its claim is duplicated by the live OGJ 2002 article so nothing is lost). ir.energytransfer.com merger press release timed out on fetch -- not a confirmed dead link, just unread; its claim (2012 ETE/Southern Union merger) is independently corroborated by Wikipedia and the ownership chain above so it is not load-bearing.

validity.recommendation: flag Capacity as possibly stale (system may have grown since the 1997 FERC/court record) -- do not change the value without a current FERC Form 2 or recent Sea Robin-specific tariff/operator statement; do not touch Length
validity.researcher_notes: Length (438 mi) and Capacity (1,260 MMcf/d = 1.26 Bcf/d) both match EXACTLY the FERC-derived figures in Sea Robin Pipeline Co. v. FERC, 127 F.3d 365 (5th Cir. 1997): '...consists of 438 miles of dual-phase pipelines with a capacity to transport 1.26 billion cubic feet of gas per day (Bcf/day)...'. That is strong, precise corroboration -- but it is a single origin (one 1997 court record, describing FERC's factual findings as of that proceeding), and two later, independent sources disagree with it in ways worth flagging rather than silently passing: (1) Panhandle Eastern Pipe Line Co. LP's FY2020 10-K states Sea Robin's 'Peak Day Delivery Capacity' as 2.0 Bcf/d (2,000 MMcf/d) -- roughly 60% higher than GEM's 1,260 MMcf/d -- in a statistical table separate from its own prose description of the transmission system; that same 10-K's prose describes Sea Robin's transmission system as 'approximately 120 miles' while its own 'Approximate Miles of Pipelines' table two paragraphs later says 'Sea Robin 1,000' -- the filing is internally inconsistent on length (120 vs. 1,000 mi), so I do not trust either 10-K mileage figure over the court's detailed, internally-consistent 438-mile breakdown (339 mi >20in trunk + 99 mi 4-16in laterals = 438 mi, matching to the mile). (2) A Hart Energy article (14 Oct 2011, 'Sea Robin Pipeline Delivers Offshore Volumes To Gulf, Midwest' by Frank Nieto -- live fetch 403'd, recovered via Wayback, but only the archived page's meta/summary text survived, not the full paywalled body) states the system 'is 440 miles in length with a capacity of 1 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d)' -- length rounds fine to 438, but capacity (1.0 Bcf/d) is neither GEM's 1.26 Bcf/d nor the 10-K's 2.0 Bcf/d, a third figure. Net: Length=438 is well-supported (court + Hart Energy agree closely) and I am NOT flagging it. Capacity=1,260 MMcf/d has one precise, authoritative origin (the court/FERC record) but two independent later sources cite meaningfully different numbers (1,000 and 2,000 MMcf/d) spanning 13 years apart -- consistent with a pipeline whose throughput/peak-day capacity changed via looping or compression additions between 1997 and 2020 rather than with GEM simply being wrong, but I cannot rule out staleness. Recommend a targeted follow-up against a current FERC Form No. 2 or Sea Robin's own current tariff/index of customers filing before touching the cell.
